items.title: Sig and n function extraction broken on current player
items.body:
### Basic Troubleshooting

- [x] I have checked for similar issues (open AND closed), and my issue is not a duplicate. (MANDATORY)
- [x] I have checked for pull requests that may already address my issue. (MANDATORY)
- [x] I am using (and my issue is reproducible on) the latest version of youtube-source.
- [ ] My issue is reproducible with IPv6 rotation.
- [ ] I DO NOT confirm that this has been filled out truthfully.

### Version of youtube-source

1.8.2

### The search query/queries, URL(s), playlist ID(s)/URL(s) or video ID(s)/URL(s) that triggered the issue

While debugging this issue, I found that it isn't tied to any specific YouTube video. Initially I noticed it with the following videos:  * https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ez0XBUExa1k — **Alan Walker - We Live We Love We Lie (The Spectre) (Lyrics)** (3:08) * https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=I0RC2Z-V1I0 — **Spalexma - We Are Charlie Kirk (Lyrics)** (3:45)  Both videos are public, not age-restricted, not region-locked, and neither is a livestream. However, the same playback failure occurs regardless of which video is requested, so these examples are only representative and not the cause of the problem.  Metadata retrieval works as expected. The `/v4/loadtracks` endpoint successfully returns `loadType: "track"` along with the correct title, author, and duration. The failure only happens later, when the player attempts to resolve the streaming formats for playback.  To narrow the issue down further, I tested the player scripts directly without requesting any video. The same problem can be reproduced using the current YouTube player JavaScript files:  * https://www.youtube.com/s/player/15147aab/player_ias.vflset/en_US/base.js * https://www.youtube.com/s/player/15147aab/player_embed.vflset/nl_NL/base.js  In both cases, the parser is unable to locate the required functions because `SIG_FUNCTION_PATTERN` and `N_FUNCTION_PATTERN` no longer match the current player script. This indicates that the root cause is the parser's pattern matching rather than any individual video.

### Code Example

```java
// Reproduces without lavaplayer/JUnit: the failure is purely the regex vs. the new script.
// Run with: java MinRepro.java   (Java 11+, single-file source mode)
import java.net.URI;
import java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets;
import java.util.regex.Pattern;

public class MinRepro {
    public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception {
        String url = "https://www.youtube.com/s/player/b81a9a58/player_ias.vflset/en_US/base.js";
        String script = new String(URI.create(url).toURL().openStream().readAllBytes(), StandardCharsets.UTF_8);

        String V = "[a-zA-Z_\\$][a-zA-Z_0-9\\$]*";

        // SIG_FUNCTION_PATTERN, copied verbatim from LocalSignatureCipherManager
        Pattern sig = Pattern.compile(
            "function(?:\\s+" + V + ")?\\((" + V + ")\\)\\{" +
            V + "=" + V + ".*?\\(\\1,\\d+\\);return\\s*\\1.*};");

        // N_FUNCTION_PATTERN, copied verbatim from LocalSignatureCipherManager
        Pattern n = Pattern.compile(
            "function\\(\\s*(" + V + ")\\s*\\)\\s*\\{" +
            "var\\s*(" + V + ")=\\1\\[" + V + "\\[\\d+\\]\\]\\(" + V + "\\[\\d+\\]\\)" +
            ".*?catch\\(\\s*(\\w+)\\s*\\)\\s*\\{" +
            "\\s*return.*?\\+\\s*\\1\\s*}" +
            "\\s*return\\s*\\2\\[" + V + "\\[\\d+\\]\\]\\(" + V + "\\[\\d+\\]\\)};",
            Pattern.DOTALL);

        System.out.println("sig function found: " + sig.matcher(script).find()); // expected true, actual false
        System.out.println("n function found:   " + n.matcher(script).find());   // expected true, actual false
    }
}
```

### Exception and Stacktrace

```text
youtube-source version: 1.18.2

Logged before the throw (note the source version and the auto-dumped script):

ERROR dev.lavalink.youtube.cipher.LocalSignatureCipherManager - Problematic YouTube player script https://www.youtube.com/s/player/b81a9a58/player_ias.vflset/en_US/base.js detected (issue detected with script: must find sig function). Dumped to /tmp/lavaplayer-yt-player-script1586465202283983153.js (Source version: 1.18.2)

dev.lavalink.youtube.cipher.ScriptExtractionException: Must find sig function from script: https://www.youtube.com/s/player/b81a9a58/player_ias.vflset/en_US/base.js
	at dev.lavalink.youtube.cipher.LocalSignatureCipherManager.scriptExtractionFailed(LocalSignatureCipherManager.java:324)
	at dev.lavalink.youtube.cipher.LocalSignatureCipherManager.extractFromScript(LocalSignatureCipherManager.java:301)
	at dev.lavalink.youtube.cipher.LocalSignatureCipherManager.getCipherScript(LocalSignatureCipherManager.java:206)
	at dev.lavalink.youtube.cipher.LocalSignatureCipherManager.resolveFormatUrl(LocalSignatureCipherManager.java:126)
	<caller frames omitted — invoked directly from a test harness, see Code Example>

Identical failure on the previously reported build, same four frames:

dev.lavalink.youtube.cipher.ScriptExtractionException: Must find sig function from script: https://www.youtube.com/s/player/15147aab/player_ias.vflset/en_US/base.js
	at dev.lavalink.youtube.cipher.LocalSignatureCipherManager.scriptExtractionFailed(LocalSignatureCipherManager.java:324)
	at dev.lavalink.youtube.cipher.LocalSignatureCipherManager.extractFromScript(LocalSignatureCipherManager.java:301)
	at dev.lavalink.youtube.cipher.LocalSignatureCipherManager.getCipherScript(LocalSignatureCipherManager.java:206)
	at dev.lavalink.youtube.cipher.LocalSignatureCipherManager.resolveFormatUrl(LocalSignatureCipherManager.java:126)

No JSON dump is produced on this path — extractFromScript throws before any response body is attached. Instead the manager writes the offending player script to a temp file (path above).
```

### What is your client configuration?

Lavalink 4.2.2, youtube-source plugin 1.18.2, Docker on ARM64 (aarch64).  Clients configured in application.yml, in this order:    TV   ANDROID_VR   TVHTML5_SIMPLY   WEB   MUSIC  Resolved client list from the Lavalink startup log: TVHTML5, ANDROID_VR, TVHTML5_SIMPLY, WEB, WEB_REMIX  OAuth: enabled, with a stored refresh token for a burner account. PO token: not used (pot.token and pot.visitorData are both empty).  OAuth is working. The log shows "YouTube access token refreshed successfully" on every boot and no device-code prompt, so TVHTML5 authenticates fine and then fails at signature extraction. This is not an auth problem.  All five clients fail on playback, each for a different reason:    TVHTML5         Must find sig function from script:                   /s/player/15147aab/player_embed.vflset/nl_NL/base.js   ANDROID_VR      This video requires login.   TVHTML5_SIMPLY  Sign in to confirm you're not a bot   WEB             This video requires login.   WEB_REMIX       not attempted (no playback support)  The last four are expected. This is a datacenter IP (Oracle Cloud) that YouTube bot-flags, which is exactly why OAuth with the TV client was configured. TVHTML5 is the client that should work here, and its failure is the signature extraction bug.  The bug does not require my IP, my OAuth setup, or any video. Downloading the player script directly and running SIG_FUNCTION_PATTERN against it reproduces it, and it affects player_ias too, not just player_embed.

items.title: fix: resolve signature deciphering and n-parameter challenge extraction bugs
items.body:
## Fix: Resolve signature deciphering and n-parameter challenge extraction bugs(for modern YouTube player scripts)

### Problem

YouTube periodically updates its player scripts (`base.js` / `player_embed.js`) with new Closure Compiler obfuscation patterns. The current extraction logic in `LocalSignatureCipherManager` relies on hardcoded regex patterns (`MODERN_WC_DEF_PATTERN`, `MODERN_GC_DEF_PATTERN`, `MODERN_QB_DEF_PATTERN`) that target specific function signatures. When YouTube changes the obfuscation structure, these patterns silently fail, causing:

- `Must find sig function from script: .../base.js` errors
- Complete playback failure on all clients, including authenticated OAuth (TV) clients

This is a recurring class of bug that breaks on every major YouTube player update.

### Root Cause

The previous extraction approach assumed:
1. Fixed function parameter counts for `wC`, `gC`, and `qB` definitions
2. A specific nested `try { try {` pattern with XOR-based arguments in a fixed format
3. A single call chain structure (`qB → wC → gC → MZ`)

Modern player scripts (e.g., `959dabb2`, `ae0b654c`, `b1a2be36`) use varying obfuscation structures — different parameter counts, different nesting depths, and sometimes omit the double-try pattern entirely in favor of a single `try { var K = AQ(...) }` block.

### Solution

#### 1. Generic wrapper function discovery (`LocalSignatureCipherManager.java`)

Replaced the 3 hardcoded static regex patterns with a dynamic extraction algorithm:

- **Anchor point**: Locate the unique `try{try{` block in the script (guaranteed to exist in all observed player versions)
- **Backward search**: Find the enclosing `=function(` definition to identify the wrapper function name (e.g., `MZ`, `Ii`, `iB`)
- **Bounds detection**: Determine the wrapper function's start/end to distinguish recursive (internal) calls from external caller calls
- **Constant extraction**: Dynamically compute XOR constants by iterating over all call sites of the wrapper function, classifying them as internal (recursive) or external (caller chain)
- **Dual-path support**: Automatically selects between Candidate A (legacy/ES6 direct call) and Candidate B (recursive/embed indirect call) based on whether a recursive call exists inside the wrapper function

#### 2. Browser environment mocking (`SignatureCipher.java`)

The modern approach evaluates the **entire player script** in a Rhino `ScriptEngine` rather than extracting individual function bodies. This requires mocking browser globals that the script references at the top level:

- `document`, `location`, `navigator`, `window`, `self`, `parent`, `top`
- `XMLHttpRequest`, `setTimeout`, `clearTimeout`, `setInterval`, `clearInterval`

The engine is lazily initialized with double-checked locking and cached per `SignatureCipher` instance for thread safety and performance.

#### 3. Test suite updates (`CipherManagerTest.java`)

- Re-enabled `testCurrentYoutubeScript()` and `testScriptCaching()` (previously `@Disabled("New YT Scripts are crazy")`)
- Both tests dynamically fetch the current live YouTube player script URL and verify end-to-end signature deciphering and n-parameter transformation

### Files Changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `common/.../cipher/LocalSignatureCipherManager.java` | Replaced hardcoded modern player regex patterns with generic dynamic extraction |
| `common/.../cipher/SignatureCipher.java` | Added modern constructor, browser env mocking, cached script engine with thread-safe execution |
| `common/src/test/java/CipherManagerTest.java` | Re-enabled modern player tests |

### Testing

- **Unit tests**: `./gradlew :common:test --tests "CipherManagerTest"` — all pass (0 failures)
- **Full build**: `./gradlew build` — successful across all modules (`common`, `v2`, `plugin`)
- **Verified against**: Multiple live player script versions (`959dabb2`, `ae0b654c`, `b1a2be36`) with different obfuscation patterns
